open_items: Out of scope, not fixed (another set): provenance/dirac_matrices/extract_from_author_notebook.wls builds the notebook path as FileNameJoin[{DirectoryName[$InputFileName], "..", ".."}]. In a deep folder on Windows that path exceeds 260 characters: 262 in scratch clone2, and FileExistsQ returned False there. The script then prints 'ERROR: author notebook not found' and exits 1. The same path without the '..' (230 characters) is found, and in a clone with a 4-character-shorter folder name (258 characters) it ran OK. A likely fix is to normalise the path (e.g. ExpandFileName or FileNameJoin of DirectoryName[$InputFileName, 3]); this belongs to the dirac-matrices provenance owner.

findings.problem: The file says test_notebook_input_cell_count 'requires ... no CR characters' and that check 6 'checks ... the line ends'. The test cannot detect CR characters. It reads the notebook with Path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), which uses universal-newline translation and turns every CR LF into LF before assertNotIn("\r", text) runs. Only the byte comparison in test_notebook_is_a_fresh_build can catch a line-end change, and that test is skipped when wolframscript is not on PATH.

findings.problem: The side-effects list leaves out temporary files. On Windows, every run of wolframscript creates two temp files in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Wolfram\WolframScript\WolframScriptTemporary\tmp_*: an empty file created when the run starts, and a file holding a copy of everything the run prints. The run does not use TEMP or TMP for these files, so the record's check (an empty private TEMP/TMP that stayed empty) cannot see them. A run that ends normally deletes both files. A run that is interrupted leaves both behind: this includes Ctrl+C, which section 3.6 itself tells the student to use when the input is missing. So 'Temporary files: none' is not true while a run is going or after an interrupted run, and the restore instructions do not cover these files.
